title_en: Chen Shuhao v. Nanjing Wuning Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. and Nanjing Qinghe Property Management Co., Ltd. — dispute over property damage compensation
ruling_gist_en: A property service enterprise has the obligation to maintain and upkeep the common areas of a residential community. It shall timely eliminate safety hazards in the common areas that may cause damage to the property of owners; otherwise, if such hazards cause damage to the owners' property, the property service enterprise shall bear liability for breach of contract and compensate the owners for their losses. Even if the safety hazard is caused by a third party, the property service enterprise's liability for breach of contract cannot be exempted. Where damage to owners' property caused by a third party's tort through the common areas of the community, the property service enterprise may be exempted from liability only if it has fulfilled its maintenance and upkeep obligations and the third party's tort was unforeseeable and unavoidable.

full_text_en:
Chen Shuhao v. Nanjing Wuning Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. and Nanjing Qinghe Property Management Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Property Damage Compensation

【Ruling Summary】

A property service enterprise has the duty to maintain and upkeep the common areas of a residential community. It shall promptly eliminate any safety hazards in such common areas that may cause damage to the property of homeowners. Otherwise, if damage to a homeowner's property occurs, the property service enterprise shall bear liability for breach of contract and compensate the homeowner for the losses. Even if the safety hazard is caused by a third party, the property service enterprise is not exempt from liability for breach of contract. Where damage to a homeowner's property caused by a third party's tort occurs through the common areas of the community, the property service enterprise may be exempted from liability only if it has fulfilled its maintenance and upkeep obligations and the third party's tort was unforeseeable and unavoidable.

Where an item of significant value is damaged, even after repair, its value may be diminished not only objectively but also in the subjective perception of people. This is value depreciation. According to the theory of liability for breach of contract, the primary method of bearing liability for breach is restitution, which necessarily requires compensation for the value depreciation of the damaged item.

A real estate development enterprise, as the seller of commercial housing, after selling the housing and transferring the ownership, and after the residential community has been enclosed, has fulfilled its obligations to the homeowners in the absence of quality defects in the sold housing and common areas, and thus shall not bear liability.

Plaintiff: Chen Shuhao, male, 30 years old, Han nationality, residing at Guangzhou Road, Gulou District, Nanjing City.

Defendant: Nanjing Wuning Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at Tianyuan Middle Road, Science Park, Jiangning District, Nanjing City.
Legal Representative: Zhao Chongxi, Chairman of the Board.

Defendant: Nanjing Qinghe Property Management Co., Ltd., domiciled at Dadongmen Commercial Pedestrian Street, Yongyang Town, Lishui County.
Legal Representative: Fu Lijuan, Chairman of the Board.

The plaintiff, Chen Shuhao, filed a lawsuit with the Nanjing Jiangning District People's Court against the defendants, Nanjing Wuning Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Wuning Company") and Nanjing Qinghe Property Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Qinghe Company"), regarding a dispute over property damage compensation.

The plaintiff, Chen Shuhao, alleged: On the morning of June 25, 2011, the wall of the Zhu Zhu Yuan area of the Wuyi Lvzhou residential community in Jiangning District, Nanjing City, developed by the defendant Wuning Company, collapsed, causing severe damage to his vehicle (license plate Su A856S3), which was parked in a designated parking space managed by the defendant Qinghe Company. After an on-site inspection, the insurance company with which the plaintiff's vehicle was insured stated that the wall collapse was caused by prolonged rainwater soaking and compression of the soil heap outside the wall, which was a human factor. Since the owner was not at fault and the responsible party for the accident could be identified, the insurance company refused compensation under the relevant insurance clauses. Subsequent investigations revealed that the wall was under the management of Wuning Company, and the collapse was due to poor management. After being informed of the situation, Wuning Company made a written undertaking to bear the plaintiff's repair costs and the cost of price assessment, but refused to compensate for the vehicle's depreciation. In this accident, Qinghe Company failed to fulfill its management responsibilities for the vehicle and should therefore also bear liability. Based on his contractual relationship with Wuning Company and Qinghe Company, the plaintiff requested: (1) the two defendants pay the plaintiff's vehicle repair costs of RMB 22,309; (2) the two defendants pay the plaintiff's price assessment fee of RMB 720; (3) the two defendants pay the plaintiff's vehicle depreciation compensation of RMB 20,000; (4) the two defendants pay the plaintiff's lost wages and transportation costs of RMB 1,000 caused by this accident; (5) the two defendants bear the litigation costs of this case; and (6) the two defendants bear joint and several liability.

The defendant Wuning Company argued: The plaintiff, Chen Shuhao, and Wuning Company have a contract for the sale of commercial housing. Wuning Company has delivered the housing and related auxiliary facilities to the plaintiff in accordance with the contract, which have passed completion inspection, and there is no breach of contract. The wall collapse was caused by a soil heap on land owned by others outside the wall, which collapsed due to heavy rain, thereby destroying the wall. It was not due to any quality defect of the wall itself. Therefore, Wuning Company has no breach of contract and bears no liability.

The defendant Qinghe Company argued: It only has a parking service agreement with the plaintiff, Chen Shuhao. According to that agreement, its company only provides order maintenance, sanitation, environmental cleaning, and parking services arising from vehicle management services for Chen Shuhao. The property rights of the residential buildings and public facilities in the community do not belong to its company. Therefore, there is no legal basis for requiring it to compensate.

The Nanjing Jiangning District People's Court found the following facts at first instance:

The plaintiff, Chen Shuhao, purchased a house (Room 906, Building 24, Zhu Zhu Yuan, Wuyi Lvzhou Community, Tianyuan Middle Road, Jiangning District, Nanjing City) developed by the defendant Wuning Company, and obtained the ownership certificate for the house in July 2009. The Zhu Zhu Yuan area has now been enclosed. On July 27, 2009, Wuning Company and the defendant Qinghe Company entered into a Wuyi Lvzhou preliminary property service contract, agreeing that Qinghe Company would provide preliminary property management services for the Wuyi Lvzhou community. The parties also agreed that Qinghe Company would carry out repair and maintenance of the common parts of the Wuyi Lvzhou community property. In December 2010, Qinghe Company and Chen Shuhao signed a parking service agreement, agreeing to allocate ground parking space No. 105 to Chen Shuhao for parking. On June 24 and 25, 2011, there was heavy rain in the area. On the morning of June 25, 2011, the soil heap piled outside the wall next to Chen Shuhao's parking space collapsed, causing the wall to fall and crush Chen Shuhao's vehicle, Su A856S3. After the vehicle was crushed, repair costs of RMB 20,654 and a price assessment fee of RMB 720 were incurred. In November 2011, Chen Shuhao filed a lawsuit with the court. During the trial, upon Chen Shuhao's application, the court commissioned the Price Certification Center of the Gulou District Price Bureau of Nanjing City to conduct an appraisal of the depreciation of the vehicle Su A856S3. The appraisal concluded that the depreciation loss of the vehicle as of June 25, 2011, was RMB 9,770.

During the trial, the plaintiff, Chen Shuhao, claimed RMB 1,000 for lost wages and transportation costs, RMB 559.83 for auto parts, and RMB 1,000 for auto detailing from the two defendants. For lost wages, he only provided a payroll sheet that did not reflect the losses caused by lost work time; for transportation costs, he only provided four taxi receipts without proving the purpose of the taxi rides; for auto parts and detailing costs, he only provided invoices without evidence showing that these expenses were caused by the vehicle damage on June 25, 2011.

The Nanjing Jiangning District People's Court held at first instance:

When the plaintiff, Chen Shuhao's, vehicle was damaged due to a tort by a third party and Chen Shuhao chose a contract claim seeking compensation for losses, the defendant Qinghe Company should bear liability for breach of contract. The reasons are as follows:

First, the cause of the damage to the plaintiff Chen Shuhao's vehicle was the defendant Qinghe Company's poor management of the common part of the community (the wall) that, according to the contract, should be managed by it. According to general circumstances and the preliminary property service contract between Qinghe Company and Wuning Company in this case, Qinghe Company has the duty to maintain and upkeep the common parts of the community, such as walls, roads, and public pipelines. Property within a community is generally divided into common parts and exclusive parts. Maintenance and repair of exclusive parts are generally the responsibility of the homeowner because the property service enterprise cannot enter or control them (with exceptions for special parts such as storage rooms with specific agreements or underground garages owned by homeowners). Maintenance and repair of common parts are usually the responsibility of the property service enterprise, as determined by the capabilities of homeowners and the property service enterprise, the division of labor in society, and contractual agreements. When a common part of the community causes damage to a homeowner's property, the property service enterprise, which has the duty to maintain and upkeep the common part, should bear liability for breach of contract. If the loss is caused by a third party's tort, the property service enterprise may recover from the third party after bearing liability for breach of contract.

Second, the defendant Qinghe Company's poor management of the common part of the community—the wall—is reflected in its failure to perform routine maintenance and upkeep of the wall. From the facts of this case, the wall collapse was caused by excessive soil accumulation outside the wall and collapse due to rain. However, based on the actual circumstances, the soil was not just piled up and then immediately collapsed in the rain. That is to say, as long as Qinghe Company had performed routine maintenance and upkeep of the wall in accordance with the contract, it could have discovered and eliminated the safety hazard, thereby preventing the damage to Chen Shuhao's vehicle.

Third, the defendant Qinghe Company argued that it only managed the order of the parking space and only owed a duty of care of an ordinary person for the safety of the parking space, and therefore disagreed with bearing liability for breach of contract. The court held that the only ground for a property service enterprise to be exempted from liability when a third party's tort against common parts of the community causes damage to a homeowner's property is that, after performing its property service obligations according to the contract, the third party's tortious act was unforeseeable and uncontrollable. A foreseeable or controllable third-party tort constitutes a safety hazard in the common parts of the community, and the property service enterprise has the duty to eliminate such hazard. The costs incurred therefrom may be borne by the third party.

Regarding the value depreciation of the plaintiff Chen Shuhao's damaged vehicle, the court held that the defendant Qinghe Company should compensate for it. So-called value depreciation refers to both the objective reduction in value of a significant item after damage, even after repair, compared to the original item, and the reduction in value in people's subjective perception. Although the latter reduction is subjective in people's minds, it objectively exists when the owner realizes the value of the item (for example, through sale). According to the theory of liability for breach of contract, when a party to a contract breaches, the primary liability to be considered is restitution. For property, restitution obviously does not only mean restoring the original physical shape of the property; it certainly includes restoring the original value of the property. Therefore, Qinghe Company should compensate Chen Shuhao for the depreciation loss of his vehicle.

Furthermore, the court also held that the defendant Wuning Company, as the seller of commercial housing, after selling the commercial housing and transferring ownership of the houses, and after the residential community was enclosed, had fulfilled its obligations to the buyer, the plaintiff Chen Shuhao, in the absence of any quality defects in the housing. Therefore, the court did not support Chen Shuhao's claim for compensation from Wuning Company. It supported Chen Shuhao's claim for compensation from the defendant Qinghe Company. The vehicle repair costs of RMB 20,654 and the price assessment fee of RMB 720 claimed by Chen Shuhao were supported by evidence such as the vehicle loss appraisal list and the price assessment fee receipt, and the court accepted them. The claims for auto parts, auto detailing, lost wages, and transportation costs were not supported because there was insufficient evidence to prove they were caused by the vehicle damage. Regarding the claimed vehicle depreciation compensation of RMB 20,000, the appraised depreciation loss was RMB 9,770, so the claim was partially supported.

Based on the above, the Nanjing Jiangning District People's Court rendered the following judgment on March 22, 2012:

First, the defendant Qinghe Company shall, within ten days from the date this judgment becomes legally effective, compensate the plaintiff Chen Shuhao for vehicle repair costs of RMB 20,654, price assessment fee of RMB 720, and vehicle depreciation compensation of RMB 9,770, totaling RMB 31,144.

Second, the plaintiff Chen Shuhao's other claims are dismissed.

Qinghe Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, arguing: (1) The legal relationship between Chen Shuhao and Qinghe Company is only a property service contract. According to Article 47 of the Property Management Regulations, the duty of care is that "a property management enterprise shall assist in doing a good job of safety prevention within the property management area." Qinghe Company only owes a duty of care of an ordinary person, meaning the property company only needs to fulfill basic safety obligations for the community and parking lot. (2) The cause of the vehicle loss due to the wall collapse was not clarified. The first-instance judgment's finding that soil was piled outside the community wall and that the wall collapsed due to heavy rain on June 25, 2011, lacks factual basis. Even if the above reasons were correct, Qinghe Company was only negligent in management and should bear only a small responsibility, not full responsibility. Therefore, the first-instance judgment should be revoked and changed to hold that Qinghe Company does not bear compensation liability, and litigation costs should be borne by Chen Shuhao.

The appellee Chen Shuhao argued: The first-instance judgment was based on facts and law. The provision in the Property Management Regulations cited by the appellant Qinghe Company is not contradictory to Qinghe Company's maintenance obligations. In summary, the first-instance court found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly, and the judgment should be affirmed.

The appellee Wuning Company argued: (1) Wuning Company has fully performed its obligations under the commercial housing sales contract with the appellee Chen Shuhao, and there is no breach of contract. It should not bear any liability for breach. The first-instance judgment correctly dismissed Chen Shuhao's claim for compensation from Wuning Company. (2) Wuning Company has entrusted the property management and services of the community in question to the appellant Qinghe Company. The responsible entity for providing property management and services to the community is Qinghe Company. Wuning Company should not bear liability for issues arising from community property services. (3) Chen Shuhao did not appeal the first-instance judgment's dismissal of his claim for compensation from Wuning Company. Therefore, the court should affirm the first-instance judgment's order dismissing Chen Shuhao's claim for compensation from Wuning Company.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, upon second-instance trial, confirmed the facts found in the first-instance trial.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court held at second instance:

A preliminary property service contract signed by the construction unit and the property service enterprise in accordance with the law is binding on the homeowners. In this case, at first instance, the appellee Chen Shuhao chose a contract claim, so this case should be a property service contract dispute. The preliminary property service contract signed between the appellee Wuning Company and the appellant Qinghe Company is legal and valid, and the parties shall perform the rights and obligations stipulated in the contract. According to the contract, Qinghe Company is responsible for the repair and maintenance of the common parts of the property. Chen Shuhao's vehicle was parked in a parking space provided by Qinghe Company and was damaged by the collapsed wall. Qinghe Company failed to fulfill its repair and maintenance obligations and should bear compensation liability. In summary, Qinghe Company's appeal requests and reasons cannot be established and are not supported.

Based on the above, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on June 19, 2012:

Appeal dismissed; judgment affirmed.

This judgment is final.
